units.title: Computer Network and Communication
topics: Concept of telecommunication: bandwidth, throughput, broadband, mobile generations (3G, 4G, 5G), data packets, frequency and communication modes (simplex, half duplex, full duplex)
Communication media: guided media (twisted pair and CAT6, coaxial, optical fibre) and unguided media (radio wave, microwave, infrared, satellite, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth)
Connectors: RJ-45, RJ-11, BNC, fibre connectors (ST, SC, SMA) and the media converter
Networking devices: NIC, repeater, hub, switch, router, modem, wireless access point and gateway
Network topology: bus, ring, star, mesh and tree/hybrid
Networks by coverage: PAN, LAN, MAN and WAN
Network architecture: client-server and peer-to-peer
IP addressing: IPv4 and IPv6, private and public addresses, static and dynamic addresses, checking an IP address and default gateway
Internet, intranet and extranet

summary: Telecommunication is exchanging information over a distance electronically; every link has a sender, message, medium, receiver and protocol.
Bandwidth is the maximum data rate of a link; throughput is the rate actually achieved; time = data in bits ÷ rate, and 1 byte = 8 bits.
Broadband (DSL, cable, fibre, satellite, wireless) is always-on and fast; 3G → 4G → 5G brought mobile Internet, then HD streaming, then very low latency for IoT. 4G reached Nepal in 2017.
Data travels in packets (header, payload, trailer). Frequency is cycles per second in hertz; λ = (c)/(f).
Modes: simplex (one way), half duplex (both ways, one at a time), full duplex (both ways together).
Guided media: twisted pair (CAT6, 100 m), coaxial, optical fibre (light, tens of km). Unguided: radio, microwave, infrared, satellite (uplink and downlink), Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, RFID.
Connectors: RJ-45 (Ethernet, 8 pins), RJ-11 (telephone), BNC (coaxial), ST, SC, LC and SMA (fibre); a media converter joins copper and fibre.
Devices: NIC (MAC address), repeater, hub (copies to all), switch (MAC, one port), bridge, router (IP, best path), modem/ONT, access point, gateway (different protocols).

summary: Data are raw facts; information is processed, meaningful data. A database is an organised collection of related data; a DBMS (MySQL, Oracle) is the software that manages it; an RDBMS keeps data in linked tables.
DBMS advantages: fast retrieval, less redundancy, consistency, security, multi-user access, backup. Disadvantages: cost, expertise, maintenance.
Data types: INT, SMALLINT, BIGINT, DECIMAL(p,s) (exact), FLOAT (approximate); CHAR(n) (fixed), VARCHAR(n) (variable), TEXT; DATE 'YYYY-MM-DD', TIME, DATETIME, TIMESTAMP; BOOLEAN = TINYINT(1).

A table has fields (columns) and records (rows). Keys: primary (unique, not NULL, one per table), candidate, alternate, composite (two or more fields), foreign (refers to another table's primary key).
Relationships: 1 : 1, 1 : M (most common), M : N (via a junction table).
Constraints: PRIMARY KEY, FOREIGN KEY, NOT NULL, UNIQUE, CHECK, DEFAULT.
DDL: CREATE, ALTER (ADD, MODIFY, CHANGE, RENAME COLUMN, DROP COLUMN), DROP, TRUNCATE, RENAME — committed at once.
DML: INSERT, SELECT (WHERE, ORDER BY ASC/DESC, LIKE with % and _), UPDATE … SET … WHERE, DELETE … WHERE. Never forget WHERE.

summary: Multimedia combines text, graphics, audio, video and animation; it may be linear or interactive and is used in education, entertainment, business, communication and content creation.

Text: serif, sans-serif and monospace fonts, size in points; typography arranges text for readability. Formats: TXT (plain), RTF (formatted), DOCX (Word), PDF (fixed layout). Use Unicode fonts for Nepali.

Raster images are grids of pixels (JPG, PNG, GIF, BMP, WebP) and pixelate when enlarged; vector images are mathematical shapes (SVG, AI, EPS) and stay sharp. Raw size = width × height × bytes per pixel.
Lossless compression keeps every detail (PNG, FLAC); lossy throws some away for small files (JPG, MP3, MP4).
Audio: amplitude = loudness, frequency = pitch; sampled at, e.g., 44,100 Hz with 16 bits. Size = rate × bits × channels × seconds. WAV is uncompressed; MP3 and AAC are compressed.
Video = frames shown at a frame rate (24, 25, 30, 60 fps) with a resolution (SD 720 × 480, HD 1280 × 720, FHD 1920 × 1080). Formats: MP4, MOV, AVI, MKV.
Tools: Pixlr (photo editing, layers, cutout; JPG/PNG/WEBP/PXZ), Canva (templates), Audacity/AudioMass (record, cut, effects, export), CapCut (timeline, trim, split, transitions, text, export MP4).
Animation: 2D (width, height) and 3D (with depth: model, rig, animate, render); frame-by-frame draws every frame, keyframe animation draws key poses and the software makes the tweens.

summary: Basics: input() returns a string, so convert with int()/float(); types int, float, str, bool, list; / gives a float, // rounds down, % gives the remainder; selection with if, if-else, if-elif-else, nested if; loops with for … in range(start, stop, step) and while.

Functions: def name(parameters): … return value. Arguments may be positional, default (rate=10, placed last) or keyword (rate=8). A void function returns None; return a, b returns a tuple. Local variables live inside a function; global ones outside.

Modules, packages, libraries: import with import m, from m import f, import m as alias. math (sqrt, pow, pi, ceil, floor, factorial, radians), random (random, randint inclusive, randrange, choice, shuffle, seed), datetime (date, timedelta, strftime); install packages with pip install.
Turtle: forward, backward, left, right, goto, penup, pendown, pensize, color, fillcolor with begin_fill/end_fill, circle, shape, speed; a regular n-gon turns 360°/n at each corner.

Errors: syntax (caught before running), runtime exceptions (ZeroDivisionError, ValueError, TypeError, NameError, IndexError, FileNotFoundError) and logical errors. try → except (on error) or else (no error) → finally (always).

Files: open(name, mode) with r, w (overwrite), a (append), x (new only); read, read(n), readline, readlines, write (no automatic newline), writelines, close, or with. CSV with the csv module or pandas.
pandas: pd.read_csv, head, shape, columns, df["col"], df[df["col"] > n] (combine with &, | and brackets), sort_values, mean, to_csv(index=False).

Matplotlib: plt.plot (trend), plt.bar (compare), plt.pie with autopct (parts of a whole), plt.scatter (relationship); add title and axis labels; plt.show(). Seaborn makes statistical charts; Plotly makes interactive ones.

summary: AI makes machines do tasks needing human intelligence; ML is AI that learns from data; deep learning and generative AI are inside ML. All present AI is narrow AI.
Learning techniques: supervised (labelled data, predicts labels), unsupervised (unlabelled data, finds groups), reinforcement (trial and error with rewards).
Robots sense (sensors), think (controller, AI) and act (actuators); simulators such as Scratch and RoboBlocky test robot programs.

Generative AI creates content from prompts: LLMs predict the next token; image generators remove noise step by step. Good prompts give task, context, format and limits. Limits: hallucination, bias, privacy, copyright, deepfakes.
AI is built into Google Docs, Gmail and Microsoft 365 (Copilot); use it with privacy, accuracy, fairness and honesty.
AI ethics: bias (fix with diverse data and human review), privacy (consent, minimal data), security (protect against hacking and poisoning).
IoT: sensors + connection + cloud + app + actuators, in smart homes, cities, farms, health, transport and schools.
VR replaces the real world; AR adds to it; MR mixes them; XR covers all three.
